figure: Figure 9.1 — Ring traffic and directional bandwidth
issue: The x-axis label says 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)', but the subtitle and caption say '140 GB tensor' without repeating 'per rank'. A reader can misread 140 GB as the total tensor size rather than the per-rank input size, which changes the arithmetic by a factor of N.
evidence: Figure subtitle: '140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75×)'. Caption: 'At 140 GB the ideal times are about 0.54 s, 6.1 s and 98 s.' The x-axis is 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)'. The 1.75× factor is 2(N−1)/N for N=8, so 140 GB must be per rank for 245 GB sent per rank to be correct.
acceptance_test: Change the subtitle and caption to say '140 GB per rank' or '140 GB logical tensor per rank' everywhere the 140 GB operating point is named; verify no remaining sentence can be read as 140 GB total.

issue: The caption's operating point is mislabeled and contradicts the book's own prose. The caption states 'At 140 GB the ideal times are about 0.55 s, 6.1 s and 98 s', but the plotted model is T = 1.75 x (logical tensor) / BW, so the values 544 ms / 6,125 ms / 98,000 ms correspond to 245 GB SENT (1.75 x 140 GB), not to a 140 GB transfer. The prose on PDF p.177 / printed p.157 gives the correct 140 GB one-way times (0.31 s NVLink, 5.6 s HDR, 56 s Ethernet). A reader who checks the caption against p.157 sees two different '140 GB' answers differing by exactly the 1.75x ring factor and cannot tell which is right.
evidence: Figure subtitle (p.178): '140 GB tensor (245 GB sent at 1.75x); NVLink 544 ms | HDR 6,125 ms | RoCE 98,000 ms'. Recomputation: 1.75 x 140 GB / 450 GB/s = 0.544 s; 1.75 x 140 / 40 = 6.125 s; 1.75 x 140 / 2.5 = 98 s. At 140 GB logical the times are 140/450 = 0.311 s, 140/40 = 3.5 s (or 5.6 s at the 25 GB/s single-port nominal used on p.157), 140/2.5 = 56 s. Caption text: 'At 140 GB the ideal times are about 0.55 s, 6.1 s and 98 s.'
acceptance_test: Caption must read 'At 245 GB sent (1.75 x the 140 GB logical tensor) the ideal times are about 0.55 s, 6.1 s and 98 s', and must add one clause stating that the 1.75x ring factor is why these exceed the one-way 140 GB times quoted on p.157 (0.31 s / 5.6 s / 56 s). A reader must be able to reconcile Fig 9.1 with the p.157 paragraph without arithmetic guesswork.

issue: The RoCE bandwidth assumption is not realizable as labeled and disagrees with the caption. The legend reads '2x5GBE RoCE: assumed effective 2.5 GB/s'. Two 5 GbE ports carry 10 Gb/s = 1.25 GB/s in aggregate, so an 'effective 2.5 GB/s' exceeds the physical link by 2x. The caption instead describes 'an assumed effective 25GbE RoCE path' (25 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s nominal, 2.5 GB/s effective = 80% efficiency, which is plausible). The legend and caption therefore specify two different fabrics for the same curve, and one of them is impossible. The related prose on PDF p.183 / printed p.163 compounds this with a unit error: '35 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s unidirectional' is false (35 Gb/s = 4.375 GB/s; 3.125 GB/s = 25 Gb/s), and 35 Gb/s is not a standard Ethernet rate.
evidence: Legend (p.178): '2x5GBE RoCE: assumed effective 2.5 GB/s'. Caption (p.178): '2.5 GB/s for an assumed effective 25GbE RoCE path'. Prose (p.183): 'Option C - 35 Gb/s Ethernet (RoCEv2) across 8 nodes. 35 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s unidirectional'. Recomputation: 2 x 5 Gb/s = 10 Gb/s = 1.25 GB/s < 2.5 GB/s; 35 Gb/s / 8 = 4.375 GB/s; 25 Gb/s / 8 = 3.125 GB/s.
acceptance_test: Legend, caption and p.183 prose must name ONE fabric with a consistent nominal rate, consistent unit conversion, and an effective value <= nominal. E.g. legend 'RoCE: 25 GbE nominal (3.125 GB/s), assumed effective 2.5 GB/s', caption matching, and p.183 corrected to '25 Gb/s = 3.125 GB/s' (or '35 Gb/s = 4.375 GB/s' with the effective value restated). A reviewer must be able to confirm effective <= nominal for every curve in the legend.

issue: The figure title 'Ring traffic and directional bandwidth' does not describe what is plotted. The axes are ideal ring completion TIME (ms) versus logical input tensor per rank (GB); bandwidth appears only as the parameter of three curves. A reader scanning the page gets no hint that the figure is a time-versus-size tradeoff, which is the figure's actual intellectual content (how ring time scales with tensor size at three bandwidths).
evidence: Figure title (p.178): 'Ring traffic and directional bandwidth'. Axes: y = 'Ideal ring completion time (ms)', x = 'Logical input tensor per rank (GB)'. Legend encodes three bandwidths.
acceptance_test: Retitle to something like 'Ideal ring all-reduce time vs per-rank tensor size at three directional bandwidths', so the title states the dependent and independent variables and the parameter.

issue: The RoCE curve (red, dotted, small markers) is the faintest element in the plot and is the curve the reader most needs to read (it is the extreme case and the one whose value the caption quotes). At print size the dotted stroke and its markers are thin relative to the solid blue curve, and the red is the lightest of the three inks, so in grayscale the RoCE curve is the least legible of the three. Dash pattern and marker shape do provide grayscale separation, so this is a polish item, not a failure of the grayscale strategy.
evidence: Rendered page 178: red dotted line with small filled markers, orange dashed with triangles, blue solid with circles. The red curve spans the full plot height (0.039 ms to 98,000 ms) and its markers are visibly smaller/thinner than the blue curve's.
acceptance_test: Increase the RoCE curve's line weight and marker size to match the blue curve's visual weight, and confirm on a grayscale proof that all three curves remain distinguishable by dash pattern plus marker shape alone.

issue: Caption formula '"In round r, rank i sends chunk (i−r) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r"' is internally inconsistent under any single round-indexing convention. With 0-indexed rounds (r=0,1,2) the formula is valid for both phases, but the reduce-scatter result is rank r retaining chunk (r+1) mod N — rank 0 would retain chunk 1 (sum=20), not the drawn chunk 0 (sum=10). With 1-indexed rounds (r=1,2,3) the formula produces the drawn intermediate state for reduce-scatter, but the all-gather fails: in round 1 rank 0 must send chunk (0−1)mod4=3, which it does not yet hold after reduce-scatter (it holds only chunk 0). The conclusion 'so rank r holds chunk r' only follows with 1-indexed rounds; 'both phases' only holds with 0-indexed rounds. The two claims cannot both be true simultaneously.
evidence: Independent rederivation, N=4, ring 0→1→2→3→0. 0-indexed: round 0 rank 0 sends c0, round 1 sends c3, round 2 sends c2 → retains c1 (sum 2+4+6+8=20 ≠ drawn 10). 1-indexed: round 1 rank 0 sends c3, round 2 sends c2, round 3 sends c1 → retains c0 (sum 1+2+3+4=10 ✓) but all-gather round 1 formula (i−1)mod4 gives rank 0 → chunk 3, which rank 0 does not hold. All-gather with 1-indexed rounds requires formula (i−r+1)modN, not (i−r)modN.
acceptance_test: Caption states the round-indexing convention explicitly and, under that single convention, the formula simultaneously (a) produces the drawn reduce-scatter intermediate state and (b) is valid for the all-gather starting state. Alternatively, caption gives separate formulas for the two phases.

issue: The annotation text '3 neighbor rounds' and '6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' is visibly smaller than the rank labels and array values and appears to fall below the 8 pt print floor at final trim size.
evidence: In the rendered 150 dpi page, the annotation text is approximately 70% the height of the main figure labels. At 150 dpi, 8 pt is about 16.7 px; these annotations appear closer to 14 px. The figure is otherwise legible, but the smallest annotations are the ones carrying the byte-count reasoning.
acceptance_test: Measure the PDF font size of the two annotation strings. If any is below 8 pt, raise it to at least 8 pt and re-render; confirm no overlap with the vertical arrows or phase labels.

issue: The caption's statement 'In round 1, rank i sends chunk (i-1) mod N in both phases' is correct for the reduce-scatter phase but wrong for the all-gather phase. In a ring all-gather, round 1 has rank i send its own chunk i to rank i+1; only in round 2 does it forward chunk (i-1) mod N. As written, the caption teaches the wrong chunk index for one of the two phases it is describing, and the figure's own 'Balanced ring neighbor order (both phases)' panel cannot disambiguate it because it shows only the neighbor order, not the chunk indices.
evidence: Caption (p.179): 'In round 1, rank i sends chunk (i-1) mod N in both phases, so rank r ends the reduce-scatter holding reduced chunk r.' Independent derivation: reduce-scatter round 1 sends chunk (i-1) mod N (rank i's chunk i-1 is the one it received last round); all-gather round 1 sends chunk i (own), round 2 sends chunk (i+1) mod N, round 3 sends chunk (i+2) mod N. The figure's per-phase byte counts (6 B sent + 6 B received per rank per phase = 3 rounds x 2 B) are consistent with either indexing, so the caption is the only place the error can live.
acceptance_test: Caption must state the chunk index per phase correctly, e.g. 'In reduce-scatter round 1, rank i sends chunk (i-1) mod N to rank i+1; in all-gather round 1, rank i sends its own chunk i to rank i+1'. Optionally add the chunk index to the ring panel so the figure carries the information rather than the caption alone.

figure: Figure 9.2 (SUM first: replication second) - caption byte accounting
issue: The caption's byte accounting does not reconcile with the figure's own annotations. As rendered, the caption reads 'Each rank sends 2 B and receives 12 B in both phases', while the figure states '6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' for each phase and 'Per rank: 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total'. The caption's 'receives 12 B' is inconsistent with the figure's 6 B received per phase (12 B received total across both phases) and with the 24 B endpoint total. If the source actually reads 'sends 2 B and receives 2 B per round in both phases', the figure and caption agree but the caption omits the word 'per round', which is exactly the distinction a reader needs (per-round 2 B vs per-phase 6 B vs per-rank 12 B). Either way the caption as printed is ambiguous or wrong on the single most quantitative claim of the figure.
evidence: Figure annotations (p.179): '3 neighbor rounds / 6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' (reduce-scatter), '3 neighbor rounds / 6 B sent + 6 B received/rank' (all-gather), 'Per rank: 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total'. Caption (p.179): 'Each rank sends 2 B and receives 12 B in both phases.' Recomputation: 3 rounds x 2 B chunk = 6 B sent per phase; 2 phases x 6 B = 12 B sent per rank; 12 B sent + 12 B received = 24 B endpoint total, matching the figure.
acceptance_test: Caption must state all three accounting levels unambiguously and consistently with the figure: 'per round, each rank sends one 2 B chunk and receives one 2 B chunk; over the 3 rounds of each phase that is 6 B sent and 6 B received per rank; across both phases, 12 B sent and 12 B received per rank (24 B endpoint total)'. Verify against the source text, not the 150 dpi render, before editing.

issue: Phase is encoded by color alone in the box borders and the two phase labels ('Reduce-scatter' in orange, 'All-gather' in blue). In grayscale the orange border and the blue border are close in value, so a grayscale reader must rely on the adjacent text labels to know which phase a row belongs to. The figure is otherwise well structured (rows are labeled, the ring panel is separate), so this is a robustness improvement rather than a defect.
evidence: Rendered page 179: input row boxes have blue borders; reduce-scatter output row boxes have orange borders; all-gather output row boxes have blue borders; the words 'Reduce-scatter' and 'All-gather' are the only non-positional cue distinguishing the two phases.
acceptance_test: Add a redundant non-color cue to the phase rows (e.g. a phase tag chip or distinct border pattern/dash) so that a grayscale print still distinguishes the reduce-scatter row from the all-gather row without relying on hue.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The text inside the layer boxes is too small for comfortable print reading. The figure packs four layers, two implementation columns, and multiple lines per box into a single page-width diagram; several box lines appear below the 8 pt floor.
evidence: At 150 dpi, the box text 'CUDA device execution', 'GPU P2P / shared memory', 'SYCL / Level Zero path', and 'Actual path depends on build' is visibly smaller than the surrounding body text and smaller than the figure's layer labels. The diagram is dense enough that the reader must work to decode the layout before understanding the payload-versus-setup distinction.
acceptance_test: Measure every text span inside the numbered layer boxes. Raise all to at least 8 pt, or split the figure into two panels (NVIDIA path and oneCCL path) with a shared setup legend. Re-render and confirm no box text is clipped or crowded.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The layer labels '1 Framework backend', '2 Collective library and algorithm', '3 Device runtime plus transport', and '4 Physical resources and topology' are left-aligned above the NVIDIA column only. They visually appear to label the left stack, not both columns, even though the right column is at the same layer.
evidence: The labels sit above the left-hand boxes and do not span or center over the two-column layout. The right-hand boxes are vertically aligned with the left-hand boxes, but the labels do not visually bind them to the same layer.
acceptance_test: Center each layer label across both columns, or add a left-margin bracket that clearly spans both columns at each numbered layer. Confirm a reader can see at a glance that ProcessGroupNCCL and ProcessGroupXCCL are both layer 1, NCCL and oneCCL are both layer 2, and so on.

figure: Figure 9.3 — The payload path is not the bootstrap path
issue: The dashed red control/setup arrows are thin and low-contrast against the light red fill of the top box. In grayscale they may read as faint gray dashes, weakening the visual separation between setup and payload.
evidence: The legend distinguishes solid black payload arrows from dashed red setup arrows. The dashed arrows from the top 'Launcher, rank/device mapping, rendezvous' box to the ProcessGroup boxes are the only red elements in the diagram and are visually lighter than the solid black payload arrows.
acceptance_test: Check the figure in grayscale at print size. If the dashed setup arrows are not immediately distinguishable from the solid payload arrows, increase their stroke weight or use a darker dash pattern while preserving the legend distinction.

figure: Figure 9.3 (The payload path is not the bootstrap path)
issue: The caption's gloss of the NCCL box conflates two distinct things. The figure's box reads 'Ring / tree / NVLS or ColNet offload'; the caption says this 'names NCCL's NVLink SHARP and ColNet in-network reduction paths'. NVLS is the NVLink SHARP transport, not the in-network reduction itself, and 'offload' is doing unstated work: the reader is left unsure whether the box means 'algorithms that offload reduction to the fabric' or 'transports that carry offloaded reduction'. The figure's own layer-3/4 boxes already separate transport from device execution, so the ambiguity is avoidable.
evidence: Figure (p.181), NCCL box: 'Ring / tree / NVLS or ColNet offload'. Caption (p.181): "The NCCL box's 'NVLS or ColNet offload' names NCCL's NVLink SHARP and ColNet in-network reduction paths, used only where the fabric and build support them (NCCL NVLS transport, pinned to v2.32.3-1; NCCL ColNet tuning, pinned to v2.32.3-1)."
acceptance_test: Caption must distinguish the reduction mechanism (NVLink SHARP, ColNet) from the transport (NVLS) and state explicitly that these entries are conditional on fabric and build support, matching the pinned versions already cited.

issue: The red dashed control path is drawn as a long routed line down the left margin to the ProcessGroupNCCL box and down the right margin to the ProcessGroupXCCL box. On the left, the dashed line runs very close to (and appears to touch) the left border of the ProcessGroupNCCL box and passes immediately beside the '1 Framework backend' heading, which weakens the visual separation between 'control/setup' and 'payload/execution' that the figure exists to establish. The right-hand dashed run also visually suggests a continuation into layers 2-4 that the figure does not actually draw.
evidence: Rendered page 181: red dashed line descends along the left edge of the figure and terminates at the left border of the ProcessGroupNCCL box; the '1 Framework backend' label sits between the dashed line and the box column.
acceptance_test: On a print proof, confirm the dashed control path does not touch or abut the ProcessGroupNCCL box border or the '1 Framework backend' heading; add clearance (or route the dashed path above the layer-1 row) so that control and payload paths are unambiguously separate. Also confirm the dashed path terminates at the layer-1 boxes only.

figure: Figure 9.1 (cross-reference: equations intended to reproduce the Fig 9.1 HDR and RoCE points)
issue: Both ring-time equations on this page fail to reproduce the values they are evidently derived from, and one of them contradicts the Fig 9.1 legend. (a) 'T_ring ~ 2*140 GB / 8*2.5 GB/s ~ 98 s' evaluates to 280/20 = 14 s, not 98 s; 98 s requires the numerator 2*(N-1)/N*140 GB = 245 GB over the per-node 2.5 GB/s, i.e. the '8' and the '2*140' are both wrong as printed. (b) 'T_ring ~ 2*(N-1)/N * M/B_eff ~ 7.140 GB / 6.1 s ~ 80 GB/s' yields 245/6.1 = 40 GB/s, not 80 GB/s, and 40 GB/s is exactly the value the Fig 9.1 legend assigns to the two-rail HDR path ('Two-rail HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'). The printed 80 GB/s therefore contradicts the figure it is meant to explain. The numerator as rendered ('7.140 GB') is also not a recognizable quantity.
evidence: p.183: 'T_ring ~ 2*(N-1)/N * M/B_eff ~ 7.140 GB / 6.1 s ~ 80 GB/s' and 'T_ring ~ 2*140 GB / 8*2.5 GB/s ~ 98 s'. Fig 9.1 legend: 'Two-rail HDR: assumed effective 40 GB/s'; Fig 9.1 subtitle: 'HDR 6,125 ms'. Recomputation: 245 GB / 6.1 s = 40.2 GB/s; 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s = 98 s; 280 GB / 20 GB/s = 14 s. The page's own downstream claims ('about 180x', '54 s, 610 s or 9,800 s') are consistent with 0.544/6.125/98 s, confirming 98 s is the intended value and the printed formula is the defect.
acceptance_test: Both equations must be rewritten so that substituting the stated inputs reproduces the printed result exactly, and the derived bandwidth must equal the Fig 9.1 legend value (40 GB/s for HDR). Specifically: T_ring ~ 2*(N-1)/N * 140 GB / 40 GB/s ~ 245 GB / 6.1 s ~ 40 GB/s, and T_ring ~ 2*(N-1)/N * 140 GB / 2.5 GB/s ~ 245 GB / 2.5 GB/s ~ 98 s. The '180x' and '54/610/9,800 s' claims must then still hold.
